summary: Someone who did not bring the korban Pesach on time brings it on Pesach Sheni, a month later. This mishnah teaches who must bring it, and why the Torah names only two kinds of people.

chunks.en: One who was tamei or on a far
chunks.st: One who was ritually impure or on a distant journey

chunks.en: journey, and did not bring the first one,
chunks.st: and did not observe the first Pesaḥ by participating in the offering of the Paschal lamb on the fourteenth of Nisan

chunks.en: should bring the second one.
chunks.st: should observe the second Pesaḥ by participating in the offering on the fourteenth of Iyyar.

words.note: Pesach Sheni, on the fourteenth of Iyar.

chunks.en: If he made a mistake or could not help it, and
chunks.st: If one unwittingly forgot or was prevented due to circumstances beyond his control and

chunks.en: did not bring the first one,
chunks.st: did not observe the first Pesaḥ,

chunks.en: he should bring the second one.
chunks.st: he too should observe the second Pesaḥ.

chunks.en: If so,
chunks.st: If so, that the second Pesaḥ is observed even by someone who forgot or was prevented from observing the first Pesaḥ,

chunks.en: why does the Torah say "tamei" or
chunks.st: why is it stated in the Torah that the second Pesaḥ is observed only by one who was ritually impure

chunks.en: "who was on a far journey"?
chunks.st: or on a distant journey?

chunks.en: To teach that these do not get kares,
chunks.explain: If they do not bring Pesach Sheni.
chunks.st: These cases were specified in order to teach that these two groups of people are exempt from karet if they do not observe the second Pesaḥ,

chunks.en: and these do get kares.
chunks.st: but those who were not ritually impure or on a distant journey are liable to receive karet, as the Gemara will explain.

summary: Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Eliezer argue what counts as a "far journey" for the korban Pesach.

chunks.en: What is a far journey?
chunks.st: What is the definition of a distant journey that exempts one from observing the first Pesaḥ?

chunks.en: From Modi'in and farther,
chunks.st: Anywhere from the city of Modi’im and beyond,

chunks.en: and the same distance in every direction.
chunks.st: and from anywhere located an equal distance from Jerusalem and beyond in every direction;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: from the doorstep of the Azarah and farther.
chunks.explain: Anyone outside the Azarah when the korban is shechted.
chunks.st: From the threshold of the Temple courtyard and beyond
chunks.stMore: is considered a distant journey;therefore, anyone located outside the courtyard at the time that the Paschal lamb is slaughtered is exempt from observing the first Pesaḥ.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said to him:

chunks.en: that is why there is a dot on the letter hei,
chunks.explain: In the Torah, the word for "far" has a dot over its hei.
chunks.st: Therefore, the word is dotted over the letter heh in the word “distant [reḥoka]”

chunks.en: to say: not because it is really far,
chunks.st: to say that the meaning of the word should be qualified: It should be understood that it is not because he is really distant;

chunks.en: but from the doorstep of the Azarah and farther.
chunks.st: rather, it includes anyone located from the threshold of the Temple courtyard and beyond.

summary: This mishnah teaches how the korban Pesach on Pesach Sheni is different from the first one, and how they are the same.

chunks.en: What is the difference between the first Pesach and the second?
chunks.st: What is the difference between the Paschal lamb offered on the first Pesaḥ and the Paschal lamb offered on the second Pesaḥ?

chunks.he: הָרִאשׁוֹן אָסוּר בְּבַל יֵרָאֶה וּבַל יִמָּצֵא,
chunks.en: On the first, having chametz is forbidden because of "it shall not be seen" and "it shall not be found."
chunks.st: On the first Pesaḥ, at the time of slaughtering the Paschal lamb, it is prohibited to own leavened bread due to the prohibitions: It shall not be seen, and: It shall not be found.

chunks.en: And on the second, he may have matzah and chametz with him in the house.
chunks.st: And on the second Pesaḥ it is permissible for one to have both leavened bread and matza with him in the house.

chunks.en: The first needs Hallel while eating it,
chunks.st: Another difference is that the Paschal lamb offered on the first Pesaḥ requires the recitation of hallel as it is eaten

chunks.en: and the second does not need Hallel while eating it.
chunks.st: and the second does not require the recitation of hallel as it is eaten.

chunks.en: Both of them need Hallel while they are made,
chunks.st: However, they are the same in that the Paschal lambs sacrificed on both the first and second Pesaḥ require the recitation of hallel as they are prepared, i.e., as they are slaughtered,

chunks.en: and they are eaten roasted with matzos and maror,
chunks.st: and they are both eaten roasted with matza and bitter herbs,

chunks.en: and they push aside Shabbos.
chunks.st: and they override Shabbat in that they may be slaughtered and their blood sprinkled even on Shabbat.

summary: When the korban Pesach is brought while most people are tamei, people with other kinds of tumah still may not eat it. This mishnah teaches what happens if they did.

chunks.en: A korban Pesach that comes in tumah,
chunks.explain: When most of the people are tamei from a dead person.
chunks.st: When the Paschal lamb is sacrificed in a state of ritual impurity due to the fact that the majority of the Jewish people are ritually impure,

chunks.en: zavim may not eat from it,
chunks.st: zavim,

words.note: People with a kind of tumah.

chunks.en: nor zavos, niddos, or women who just had a baby.
chunks.st: and zavot, and menstruating women, and women after childbirth may not eat it, because the Paschal lamb overrides only ritual impurity imparted by a corpse, but it does not override other forms of ritual impurity.

words.note: Women with a kind of tumah.

chunks.en: But if they ate,
chunks.st: However, if they violated the halakha and ate from the offering,

chunks.en: they do not get kares.
chunks.st: they are exempt from karet.
chunks.stMore: One who eats sacrificial food in a state of ritual impurity is generally liable to receive karet; however, since in this case the offering is sacrificed in a state of ritual impurity, there is no punishment of karet even for ritually impure individuals who are not permitted to eat it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer frees them even
chunks.st: And Rabbi Eliezer exempts these individuals from karet

chunks.en: for going into the Beis Hamikdash.
chunks.st: even for entering the Temple in a state of ritual impurity,
chunks.stMore: despite their not being permitted to enter, because people who are impure due to ritual impurity imparted by a corpse are permitted to enter the Temple in this situation despite their impurity.

summary: This mishnah teaches how the korban Pesach in Mitzrayim was different from the korban Pesach of all later years.

chunks.he: מַה בֵּין פֶּסַח מִצְרַיִם לְפֶסַח דּוֹרוֹת,
chunks.en: What is the difference between the Pesach of Mitzrayim and the Pesach of the generations?
chunks.st: What are the differences between the Paschal lamb that the Jewish people offered in Egypt and the Paschal lamb offered in all later generations?

chunks.en: The Pesach of Mitzrayim was taken on the tenth,
chunks.st: The Paschal lamb the Jewish people offered in Egypt had to be taken from the tenth of the month of Nisan

chunks.en: and it needed sprinkling with a bunch of hyssop on
chunks.st: and required the people to sprinkle its blood with a bundle of hyssop, unlike the Paschal lamb in all later years, and its blood was also sprinkled

chunks.en: the top of the door and on the two doorposts,
chunks.st: upon the lintel and the two doorposts,

chunks.en: and it was eaten in a hurry, on one night.
chunks.st: and it was eaten with haste; in addition, the Paschal lamb in Egypt was only on one night,

chunks.en: But the Pesach of the generations lasts all seven days.
chunks.explain: No chametz is allowed all seven days.
chunks.st: whereas the Paschal lamb throughout the generations is observed for seven days.

summary: Rabbi Yehoshua heard two different rules about an animal swapped for a korban Pesach, and Rabbi Akiva explains when each one is true.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said:

chunks.en: I heard that the swap of a korban Pesach is offered,
chunks.st: I heard two rulings from my teachers: One ruling was that the substitute of a Paschal lamb is sacrificed as a peace-offering after Passover,

words.note: An animal someone tried to swap for a korban. It also becomes holy.

chunks.en: and that the swap of a korban Pesach is not offered,
chunks.st: and another ruling was that the substitute of a Paschal lamb is not sacrificed as a peace-offering after Passover;

chunks.en: and I can't explain it.
chunks.st: and I cannot explain these two rulings,
chunks.stMore: as I do not remember the circumstances to which each ruling applies.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said:

chunks.en: I will explain.
chunks.st: I will explain:

chunks.en: A korban Pesach that was lost and found before the korban Pesach was shechted,
chunks.explain: He had already set aside another one in its place.
chunks.st: With regard to a lamb that is separated as a Paschal lamb and is then lost, leading the owner to separate another animal as its replacement, and is later found before the slaughter of the replacement Paschal lamb,

chunks.en: it should graze until it gets a mum,
chunks.st: it is left to graze until it becomes unfit [yista’ev] and disqualified for use as a sacrifice.

chunks.en: and be sold, and he buys a shelamim with its money.
chunks.st: It is then sold and becomes unconsecrated, and the owner must bring a peace-offering with its proceeds.

chunks.en: And the same for its swap.
chunks.st: And so too, the same is true with regard to its substitute:
chunks.stMore: If one separates another lamb as a substitute for this replacement, the sanctity of the original lamb extends to the substitute as well. In the case outlined above, the substitute would graze, just like the replacement, until it developed a blemish and would then be sold. This is the circumstance in which the substitute of a Paschal lamb is not sacrificed.

chunks.en: After the korban Pesach was shechted,
chunks.st: On the other hand, if the lost lamb is found after the slaughter of the replacement Paschal lamb,

chunks.en: it is offered as a shelamim,
chunks.st: it itself is sacrificed as a peace-offering,

chunks.en: and the same for its swap.
chunks.st: and so too, its substitute is sacrificed, which explains the ruling that the substitute of a Paschal lamb is sacrificed as a peace-offering.

summary: This mishnah teaches what to do with an animal that cannot be a korban Pesach, and with a korban Pesach whose owner died.

chunks.en: One who sets aside a female for his korban Pesach, or
chunks.explain: The korban Pesach must be a male.
chunks.st: In the case of one who separates a female animal for his Paschal lamb although the Torah requires a male,

chunks.en: a male in its second year,
chunks.explain: It must be in its first year.
chunks.st: or a male that is in its second year although a Paschal lamb must be an animal that is in its first year,

chunks.en: it should graze until it gets a mum,
chunks.st: the animal is left to graze until it develops a blemish and becomes unfit,

chunks.en: and be sold, and its money goes for nedavah korbanos.
chunks.st: and it is then sold and its money is used for free-will offerings or peace-offerings.

words.note: Korbanos given just because one wants to.

chunks.en: One who set aside his korban Pesach and died,
chunks.st: With regard to one who separates his Paschal lamb and then dies,

chunks.he: לֹא יְבִיאֶנּוּ בְנוֹ אַחֲרָיו לְשֵׁם פֶּסַח,
chunks.en: his son after him should not bring it as a korban Pesach,
chunks.st: his son may not bring it after him for the purpose of a Paschal lamb because it may no longer be used for that purpose after its owner has died.

chunks.en: but as a shelamim.
chunks.st: Rather, it is brought for the purpose of a peace-offering.

summary: This mishnah teaches what to do if a korban Pesach got mixed up with other korbanos, or with bechoros.

chunks.en: A korban Pesach that got mixed up with other korbanos,
chunks.st: In the case of a Paschal lamb that was intermingled with other offerings,
chunks.stMore: such as guilt-offerings and burnt-offerings, and it is not known which animal was separated for which offering,

chunks.en: all of them should graze until they get a mum,
chunks.st: all of them are left to graze until they develop a blemish and become unfit;

chunks.he: וְיִמָּכְרוּ, וְיָבִיא בִדְמֵי הַיָּפֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן מִמִּין זֶה,
chunks.en: and be sold, and with the money of the best of them he brings one of this kind,
chunks.st: and they are then sold, and with the proceeds of the choicest of them he must bring this type of sacrifice,

chunks.en: and with the money of the best of them one of this kind,
chunks.explain: For each kind, he pays the price of the most expensive animal.
chunks.st: and with the proceeds of the choicest of them he must bring this other type of sacrifice,
chunks.stMore: meaning that he must purchase one of each type of sacrifice that was intermingled at the value of the most expensive animal in the group.

chunks.en: and he loses the extra from his own pocket.
chunks.st: And he loses the difference from his own pocket.
chunks.stMore: Not all the offerings were as expensive as the most valuable animal in the group, yet he must purchase an animal for each type of offering for the value of the most expensive animal in the group.

chunks.en: If it got mixed up with bechoros,
chunks.st: If a Paschal lamb was intermingled with firstborn animals,

words.note: Firstborn animals, given to the Kohanim.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: if they are a group of Kohanim, they may eat them.
chunks.st: If those whose offerings became mixed together were groups of priests, they may eat all of the animals on Passover night.
chunks.stMore: This is because priests are permitted to eat the meat of a firstborn animal, and the slaughter and other services for a firstborn animal are the same as those for a Paschal lamb. The attending priests should state that they intend to sacrifice as a Paschal lamb whichever animal is the Paschal lamb and to sacrifice as a firstborn animal whichever animal is a firstborn.

summary: A group's korban Pesach got lost and one of them went to look for it, while the others shechted a new one. This mishnah teaches who eats from which korban, depending on what they told each other.

chunks.en: A group whose korban Pesach got lost,
chunks.st: With regard to a group whose Paschal lamb was lost,

chunks.en: and they said to one of them,
chunks.st: and they said to one member of the group:

chunks.en: "Go and look for it, and shecht it for us,"
chunks.st: Go and search for our Paschal lamb, and when you find it, slaughter it on our behalf;

chunks.en: and he went and found it and shechted it,
chunks.st: and he went and found the missing offering and slaughtered it on behalf of the entire group,

chunks.en: and they took another one and shechted it:
chunks.st: but in the meantime they took a different animal and slaughtered it as a Paschal lamb, the halakha is as follows:

chunks.en: if his was shechted first,
chunks.st: If his Paschal lamb was slaughtered first,

chunks.en: he eats from his,
chunks.st: he eats from his offering, as he is considered to be registered specifically for that offering,

chunks.en: and they eat with him from his.
chunks.st: and they eat with him from his offering, because he included them in his offering and it belongs to the entire group.
chunks.stMore: The second animal does not have any registrants and is therefore burned.

chunks.en: And if theirs was shechted first,
chunks.st: And if theirs was slaughtered first,

chunks.en: they eat from theirs,
chunks.st: they eat from theirs
chunks.stMore: because they withdrew from the original offering through the act of slaughtering a replacement,

chunks.en: and he eats from his.
chunks.st: and he eats from his because he was not registered for the replacement offering sacrificed by the remainder of his group.

chunks.en: And if it is not known which
chunks.st: And if it is not known which of the offerings

chunks.en: of them was shechted first,
chunks.st: was slaughtered first,

chunks.en: or if both were shechted together,
chunks.st: or if both the group and the individual slaughtered them together,

chunks.en: he eats from his,
chunks.st: he eats from his

chunks.en: and they do not eat with him,
chunks.st: and they do not eat with him in case theirs was slaughtered first,

chunks.en: and theirs goes out to the place of burning,
chunks.st: and theirs must be taken out to the place designated for burning.
chunks.stMore: The offering slaughtered by the group may not be eaten due to the concern that it was slaughtered second and the members of the group would therefore have been included in the first offering.

chunks.en: and they do not need to bring Pesach Sheni.
chunks.st: However, they are exempt from performing the offering of the Paschal lamb on the second Pesaḥ,
chunks.stMore: because they were included in the slaughter of whichever animal was slaughtered first. It is only due to external circumstances that they cannot complete the mitzva by eating the Paschal lamb, and this does not prevent them from fulfilling their obligation.

chunks.en: If he said to them,
chunks.st: A somewhat different case of a lost Paschal lamb would occur if the group had sent one member as an agent to search for the lost animal, and the agent said to the other members of the group before he left:

chunks.en: "If I am late,
chunks.st: If I am late,

chunks.en: go and shecht for me,"
chunks.st: go and slaughter a Paschal lamb for me.

chunks.en: and he went and found it,
chunks.st: He then went and found the lost Paschal lamb

chunks.en: and shechted it, and they took another one and shechted it:
chunks.st: and slaughtered it, and they took another animal and slaughtered it as a Paschal lamb.

chunks.en: if theirs was shechted first,
chunks.st: In that case, if theirs was slaughtered first,

chunks.en: they eat from theirs,
chunks.st: they eat from theirs

chunks.en: and he eats with them.
chunks.st: and he eats with them,
chunks.stMore: because he requested to be included in their offering and they registered him for their Paschal lamb.

chunks.en: And if his was shechted first,
chunks.st: And if his was slaughtered first,

chunks.en: he eats from his,
chunks.st: he eats from his

chunks.en: and they eat from theirs.
chunks.st: and they eat from theirs,
chunks.stMore: because the fact that they slaughtered a different animal indicates that they have withdrawn from the original offering.

chunks.en: And if it is not known which
chunks.st: And if it is not known which of the animals

chunks.en: of them was shechted first,
chunks.st: was slaughtered first,

chunks.en: or if both were shechted together,
chunks.st: or if both the group and the individual slaughtered them together,

chunks.en: they eat from theirs,
chunks.st: they eat from theirs
chunks.stMore: because they definitely withdrew from the original offering by slaughtering a different one,

chunks.en: and he does not eat with them,
chunks.st: and he does not eat with them
chunks.stMore: because he also intended to be included in the animal he slaughtered and it is not clear which was slaughtered first.

chunks.en: and his goes out to the place of burning,
chunks.st: Therefore, his must be taken out to the place designated for burning;

chunks.en: and he does not need to bring Pesach Sheni.
chunks.st: and he is exempt from performing the sacrifice of the Paschal lamb on the second Pesaḥ.

chunks.en: If he said to them and they said to him,
chunks.st: If he said to them that if he is delayed they should include him in their Paschal lamb, and they said to him that if he finds the original offering he should slaughter it on their behalf,

chunks.en: they all eat from the first one.
chunks.st: all of them eat from the first sacrifice that was slaughtered.

chunks.en: And if it is not known which
chunks.st: And if it is not known which of them

chunks.en: of them was shechted first,
chunks.st: was slaughtered first,

chunks.en: both of them go out to the place of burning.
chunks.st: both of them must be taken out to the place designated for burning, and the entire group is exempt from participating in the Paschal lamb on the second Pesaḥ.

chunks.he: לֹא אָמַר לָהֶן וְלֹא אָמְרוּ לוֹ,
chunks.en: If he did not say to them and they did not say to him,
chunks.st: If he did not say anything to them and they did not say anything to him, meaning that neither side granted the other authority to slaughter a Paschal lamb on its behalf,

chunks.en: they are not responsible for each other.
chunks.explain: Each one eats from his own korban.
chunks.st: they are not responsible for each other,
chunks.stMore: and the members of the group eat their Paschal lamb while the individual sent to find the lost animal eats from his own offering. The reason for this is that the individual is registered only for the original offering, while the other members of the group withdrew from that lost offering by sacrificing a different Paschal lamb.

summary: Two groups' korbanos Pesach got mixed up and nobody knows which is whose. This mishnah teaches how they swap members so that everyone ends up signed up on the right korban.

chunks.en: Two groups whose korbanos Pesach got mixed up:
chunks.st: Two groups whose Paschal lambs have become intermingled
chunks.stMore: and they do not know which one belongs to which group should act in the following manner:

chunks.en: these take one for themselves
chunks.st: These members of the first group draw one of the animals separated as a Paschal lamb for themselves,

chunks.en: and these take one for themselves.
chunks.st: and those members of the second group draw one for themselves.

chunks.he: אֶחָד מֵאֵלּוּ בָא לוֹ אֵצֶל אֵלּוּ,
chunks.en: One of these comes over to those,
chunks.st: One of these, a member of one group, comes to those, the members of the other group,

chunks.he: וְאֶחָד מֵאֵלּוּ בָא לוֹ אֵצֶל אֵלּוּ,
chunks.en: and one of those comes over to these.
chunks.st: and one of those members of the second group comes to these members of the first group.

chunks.en: And this is what they say:
chunks.st: And this is what each group says to the member of the other group who has come to join them:

chunks.en: "If this korban Pesach is ours,
chunks.st: If this Paschal lamb that is now in our possession is ours,

chunks.he: יָדֶיךָ מְשׁוּכוֹת מִשֶּׁלְּךָ וְנִמְנֵיתָ עַל שֶׁלָּנוּ,
chunks.en: your hands are pulled away from yours and you are signed up on ours.
chunks.st: you are withdrawn from the Paschal lamb that was yours, and you are registered for our Paschal lamb and you may eat from it.

chunks.en: And if this korban Pesach is yours,
chunks.st: And if this Paschal lamb is yours, meaning that it actually belongs to the other group, including this individual,

chunks.he: יָדֵינוּ מְשׁוּכוֹת מִשֶּׁלָּנוּ וְנִמְנֵינוּ עַל שֶׁלָּךְ.
chunks.en: our hands are pulled away from ours and we are signed up on yours."
chunks.st: we are hereby withdrawn from ours and we are registered for your Paschal lamb, which you agree to share with us.
chunks.stMore: The other group makes the same statement.

chunks.he: וְכֵן חָמֵשׁ חֲבוּרוֹת שֶׁל חֲמִשָּׁה חֲמִשָּׁה,
chunks.en: And so too five groups of five people each,
chunks.st: And similarly, if there were five groups of five people each

chunks.en: or of ten people each,
chunks.st: or of ten people each,

chunks.he: מוֹשְׁכִין לָהֶן אֶחָד מִכָּל חֲבוּרָה וַחֲבוּרָה,
chunks.en: they take one from each and every group,
chunks.st: they draw one person from each and every group,

chunks.en: and they say the same thing.
chunks.st: and they say this statement mentioned in the case of two groups.
chunks.stMore: The remaining member or members of each group will grant the representatives of the other groups that have come to join them a share in the Paschal lamb, and they will acquire a share in it for themselves in case the animal they have chosen belonged originally to one of the other groups.

summary: Two people's korbanos Pesach got mixed up. This mishnah teaches how each one adds a new person, so they can swap and both be signed up on the right korban.

chunks.en: Two people whose korbanos Pesach got mixed up:
chunks.st: In the case of two individuals whose Paschal lambs became intermingled
chunks.stMore: and each person was the only one registered for his offering, what should they do?

chunks.en: this one takes one for himself,
chunks.st: This person draws one of the Paschal lambs for himself

chunks.en: and that one takes one for himself.
chunks.st: and that person draws one for himself;

chunks.he: זֶה מַמְנֶה עִמּוֹ אֶחָד מִן הַשּׁוּק,
chunks.en: This one signs up one person from the market with him,
chunks.st: this person registers someone from the marketplace with him on his Paschal lamb

chunks.he: וְזֶה מַמְנֶה עִמּוֹ אֶחָד מִן הַשּׁוּק,
chunks.en: and that one signs up one person from the market with him.
chunks.st: and that person registers someone from the marketplace with him on his Paschal lamb.

chunks.en: This one comes to that one,
chunks.st: Once this has been done, this one comes to that person from the marketplace who has been added to the other person’s sacrifice,

chunks.en: and that one comes to this one,
chunks.st: and that one comes to this person from the marketplace who has been added to the first person’s sacrifice,

chunks.en: and this is what they say:
chunks.st: and this is what they say:

chunks.en: "If this korban Pesach is mine,
chunks.st: If this Paschal lamb is mine,

chunks.he: יָדֶיךָ מְשׁוּכוֹת מִשֶּׁלְּךָ וְנִמְנֵיתָ עַל שֶׁלִּי.
chunks.en: your hands are pulled away from yours and you are signed up on mine.
chunks.st: you are withdrawn from yours and you are registered for mine,

chunks.en: And if this korban Pesach is yours,
chunks.st: and if this is your Paschal lamb,

chunks.he: יָדַי מְשׁוּכוֹת מִשֶּׁלִּי וְנִמְנֵיתִי עַל שֶׁלָּךָ:
chunks.en: my hands are pulled away from mine and I am signed up on yours."
chunks.st: I am withdrawn from mine and I am hereby registered for yours,
chunks.stMore: as described previously. The reason it is necessary for each individual to add an additional person to his Paschal lamb, is to ensure that when each person withdraws from his original Paschal lamb and registers for the other, no Paschal lamb will be left ownerless for any amount of time.
